boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Gannon rituals and recurring events, from a first-year common read and two service days to a locally crafted ceremonial mace.

cards.title: Follow a Mace Made From Gannon Relics
cards.subtitle: A new annual commencement ritual carrying pieces of Gannon history
cards.notes: At commencement, watch the Faculty Senate president lead the procession with a mace incorporating chapel brass and wood representing Erie and Ruskin.
cards.short_summary: Gannon turned centennial materials and institutional symbols into an annual academic-procession object.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon says its Makerspace created the centennial mace with brass from Mary, Seat of Wisdom Chapel, replicas from Archbishop Gannon’s chalice, and wood representing Erie and Ruskin; the Faculty Senate president will carry it at commencement each year.
cards.source_title: Gannon creates new commencement tradition with centennial mace
cards.access_notes: This ceremonial practice occurs during Gannon commencement; attendance and graduate instructions vary by ceremony.

cards.title: Volunteer Everywhere on GIVE Day
cards.subtitle: Gannon’s annual fall service day meets the International Coastal Cleanup
cards.notes: Register through Gannon, attend the Erie kickoff, then serve at your assigned community site; project locations and duties change each year.
cards.short_summary: The Gannon community fans out across Erie and beyond for one coordinated September service day.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon documents GIVE Day—Gannon’s Invitation to Volunteer Everywhere—as an annual service event held at its Erie and Ruskin campuses and timed to coincide with the International Coastal Cleanup.
cards.source_title: Gannon spends Saturday giving back to Erie and Ruskin communities
cards.access_notes: Participation uses assigned service locations; consult the current event registration for eligibility, check-in, clothing and transportation details.

cards.title: Spring-Clean the Community on Day of Caring
cards.subtitle: Gannon’s annual spring service tradition aligned with Earth Week
cards.notes: Choose an official project and arrive prepared for its stated task, which may include painting, park cleanup or nonprofit support.
cards.short_summary: Gannon marks spring with a coordinated day devoted to practical work for community partners.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon identifies Day of Caring as an annual event organized by its Center for Social Concerns; the spring service day coincides with Earth Week and involves students, faculty and staff.
cards.source_title: Gannon’s Day of Caring mobilizes nearly 600 volunteers across three states
cards.access_notes: Projects occur at multiple community sites and may be outdoors; follow the current organizer’s registration, weather and accessibility guidance.

cards.title: Put a Year of Work on Display
cards.subtitle: An annual showcase for Gannon research, scholarship, engagement and art
cards.notes: Browse the presentation program before attending, then ask student presenters about the methods, community partners or creative process behind their work.
cards.short_summary: Students convert research and creative collaborations into a university-wide public showcase.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon describes Celebrate Gannon as an annual event featuring research, scholarship, engagement and fine-art collaborations by students with faculty and staff, including a continuing digital presentation book.
cards.access_notes: Dates, presentation locations and viewing formats vary annually; consult the current Celebrate Gannon program.

cards.entity_name: Dr. David and MaryAnne Kozak Gannon READS Program
cards.title: Start Gannon With One Shared Book
cards.subtitle: First-year students read and discuss a common selection before an author visit
cards.notes: Read the selected book before the fall lecture, bring a discussion question and compare its themes with conversations from Gannon 101.
cards.short_summary: A common book links first-year coursework to a campus author conversation and public lecture.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon says its READS program gives first-year students a common book to read and discuss, invites the author to meet students in fall, and culminates in an evening lecture open to Gannon and Erie communities.
cards.source_title: The Dr. David and MaryAnne Kozak Gannon READS Program
cards.access_notes: The selected title, author, lecture date and venue change by year; use the program page for the current details.

cards.title: Receive the Class Book at Convocation
cards.subtitle: Incoming students begin a shared reading ritual before Gannon 101 discussions
cards.notes: Pick up the class selection at Student Convocation, note the fall discussion schedule and keep the book ready for your Gannon 101 sessions.
cards.short_summary: Student Convocation doubles as the handoff point for the first-year class’s shared text.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon reports that each incoming first-year student received the selected Gannon READS book at Student Convocation and then discussed it in Gannon 101 during the fall semester.
cards.source_title: Gannon READS lecture to welcome Author David LaMotte
cards.access_notes: This practice is tied to incoming first-year programming; confirm the current convocation and course arrangements with Gannon.

cards.title: See Erie’s Cultures Share One Stage
cards.subtitle: A recurring Gannon-hosted dance program built with local performers
cards.notes: Review the announced cultures and ensembles, attend the staged program and join any audience participation only when performers invite it.
cards.short_summary: Gannon and Erie artists make cultural dance the focus of an evolving community-stage tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon hosted Multicultural Dance Night for the fourth time in 2026, featuring Erie-area artists performing dances representing multiple cultures as part of the university’s CHESS Speaker Series.
cards.source_title: Gannon celebrates Erie’s rich tapestry of cultures at Multicultural Dance Night
cards.access_notes: Venue, performers, ticketing and participation format can change; consult the current CHESS Speaker Series listing.

cards.title: Read Across Majors at Writing Awards Night
cards.subtitle: An annual ceremony recognizing research writing, journalism and poetry
cards.notes: Look for the current call for submissions, follow its category rules and attend the ceremony to hear work recognized across Gannon’s colleges.
cards.short_summary: Gannon gathers writers from varied disciplines for a long-running night of readings and recognition.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s CHESS Speaker Series states that the university celebrates an annual Writing Awards Program recognizing students from all three academic colleges for research writing, journalism and poetry.
cards.access_notes: Submission eligibility, categories, ceremony date and venue are announced for each annual program.

cards.title: Start Homecoming at the Family Tailgate
cards.subtitle: Golden Knight games follow a campus gathering of alumni, students and families
cards.notes: Check the Homecoming schedule, meet your group at the designated tailgate area and leave enough time to reach the day’s football or soccer match.
cards.short_summary: Gannon’s Homecoming crowd gathers before shifting from the tailgate to Golden Knight athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s 2025 Centennial Homecoming program documented a Homecoming Family Tailgate before Golden Knight football and soccer games, within a weekend bringing together alumni, students, employees and families.
cards.source_title: Gannon University welcoming alumni, family, friends to celebrate Centennial Homecoming and Family Weekend
cards.access_notes: Tailgate site, admission, registration and game tickets vary by Homecoming year; follow the current official schedule.

cards.title: Take the Campus Plunge for Special Olympics
cards.subtitle: A themed cold-water fundraiser staged beneath the Gannon Arch
cards.notes: Register through the official fundraiser, meet its participation requirements and bring dry clothes before entering the supervised mobile plunge unit.
cards.short_summary: Gannon turns a mobile cold-water tank beneath its arch into a visible Special Olympics fundraiser.
cards.evidence_claim: In 2026, Gannon held the Bear Force One Polar Plunge under the Gannon Arch as a Special Olympics Pennsylvania fundraiser, with students, faculty and staff entering a mobile plunge unit.
cards.source_title: Gannon raises $11K for Special Olympics with campus Polar Plunge
cards.access_notes: Participation may require registration and fundraising; use only the organized mobile plunge and follow current safety instructions.
